test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: After fertilization, what will be the future of these parts of a flower- stamens, style, stigma, petal and sepal?

options.text: Stigma, style, stamen shed off except petal and sepal in some plants
Stigma, style shed off except stamen, petal and sepal
They shed off except sepal which may be persistent in some plants
Persistent except sepal shed off in mostly plants

solution:
The correct answer is __**They shed off except sepal which may be persistent in some plants**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After fertilization, **the parts of a flower that usually fall off are the petals, stamens, style, and stigma, except for the sepals in some cases**.
 
• The sepals **may shrivel up or dry up, but stay with the fruit.**
 
• For example,** in guavas, the sepals are extremely dry, while in tomatoes, they shrivel up, and in brinjals, they are intact and green**
 
• **Things that happen to a flower after fertilization: **
 
 
• The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit.
 
• The zygote **divides and develops into an embryo.**
 
• **The ovules develop into seeds.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fertilization of Flower
 
 
• In fertilization of a flower, one sperm nucleus fertilizes the egg cell, forming a zygote, while the other sperm nucleus usually fuses with the binucleate central cell, forming a primary endosperm cell (its nucleus is often called the triple fusion nucleus). That cell created in the process of double fertilization develops into the endosperm.
 
• The most important and unique characteristic of angiosperms is the participation of both male gametes in the act of fertilization. One male gamete fuses with the egg cell and forms the diploid Zygote. The process is called syngamy or generative fertilization. The Zygote (2n) develops into an embryo.
 
• The other male gamete fuses with two polar nuclei (or secondary nuclei) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus. The process is known as triple fusion or Vegetative fertilization. 
 
• These two actions of fertilization are together called Double Fertilization
